name: Battle of Yamen

phases.title: The chained Song fleet and the four Yuan parts
phases.text: The Song ships lay chained in a long string in the bay, with the emperor's boat in the middle. Zhang Hongfan split his ships into four parts: three for the Song's east, north and south sides, and one under his own command a short way off.

phases.title: The north flank is repulsed
phases.text: The Yuan north squadron engaged the Song fleet first and was driven back. The Song ships stayed chained where they lay, and the rest of the Yuan force held its places.

phases.title: Zhang Hongfan attacks from the front
phases.text: After the Yuan played festive music, which led the Song to think they were feasting, Zhang Hongfan attacked from the front with more soldiers hidden under cloth. Waves of arrows hit the Song ships, and seven ships were lost at once.

phases.title: Zhang Shijie tries to break out
phases.text: The chained Song ships could neither support the middle nor retreat, and command broke down. Zhang Shijie cut about a dozen ships from the formation in an attempt to save the emperor.

phases.title: The Yuan reach the emperor's boat
phases.text: The Yuan advanced quickly to the centre and to Zhao Bing, killing everyone in their way. Lu Xiufu took the boy emperor and jumped into the sea, and both drowned. Zhang Shijie escaped the battle.

note: The plan shows the Song fleet and the Yuan squadrons in the bay. The accounts give the Song fleet as one chained string with the emperor's boat in the middle; it is drawn here as two halves either side of that boat. They give no compass directions, so the squadrons' sides are drawn as north, east and south on the page and Zhang Hongfan's own force on the west, where the accounts say only that it stood about a li from the Song forces. The direction of the breakout is not given.
